Hi Jordan —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Summary + next steps below; Neha from our security team is looped for technical details. I've attached a high-level SOC 2 summary and our retention matrix to this thread for your review.

Quick answers up front (defaults):
- Application data deletions: processed within 72 hours from request; primary records removed and marked for cascading deletion across services.
- Backups & snapshots: default retention 30 days; backups are scheduled for purge as part of our retention lifecycle. In many cloud providers immutable snapshots are removed via an automated purge job; we can provide confirmation when purge completes.
- Logs: application logs (90 days default); audit/security logs (365 days default).
- SOC 2: We have a SOC 2 Type II report; summary attached. Full report available under NDA — we can start an NDA now or provide via your secure portal.

We can also accelerate backup purge to a contractually guaranteed 7-day window (expedited purge workflow) if that is required for your use case — that would be added as a contractual SLA.

Next steps:
1) Neha, can you add the deletion propagation steps and backup purge detail?
2) Jordan — confirm if you need the 7-day expedited backup purge or standard 30-day default.
3) We'll send a vendor questionnaire link (DocuSign/secure form) once you confirm.

Files attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, retention_matrix.csv

Best,

Thanks Marissa — quick clarifications from our security team: 

- When you say backups are scheduled for purge as part of retention lifecycle, does a user-initiated deletion trigger immediate tombstoning only, or does it enqueue a removal request for all backup copies and immutable snapshots? We need to understand the timeline for full irrevocable removal.
- For immutable snapshots (cloud-provider snapshots), what is your runbook to request deletion? How long do providers typically take to remove those snapshots?
- For audit/evidence purposes, can you provide a description or artifact showing the backup deletion pipeline and where an internal operator or automation confirms purge completion?
- For logs, we need separation between application logs (for analytics) and security/audit logs (for compliance). Can you confirm default retention and whether audit logs can be exported to our SIEM before deletion?

If you can provide a short write-up or diagram and start the vendor questionnaire that would be ideal. Our deadline for procurement sign-off is Nov 10.

—Jordan (on behalf of Amaya InfoSec)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Amaya Security <security@amaya.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data retention & deletion SLAs (post-demo)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks — happy to lay out the technical details. Below is the current behavior and the contractual options we can offer: 

1) Deletion propagation (primary data):
- When a deletion request is submitted (API/console/DSAR), the primary records are removed or cryptographically shredded within 72 hours. Deletion is recorded in our audit logs with a deletion request ID.

2) Backups & immutable snapshots:
- Default: backups (regular and snapshot-based) are retained 30 days. Backups are managed by our backup pipeline which runs daily; retention windows are enforced by automated jobs that permanently remove objects once their retention window expires.
- User-initiated deletions enqueue a purge request for related backup objects. In practice, purge will occur as soon as the backup object's retention window allows — typically up to 30 days after the original deletion unless an expedited purge SLA is contracted.
- Immutable snapshots managed by cloud providers (e.g., provider EBS/Azure snapshots) are removed via our provider API calls. For most major providers we observe removal confirmation within 48–168 hours (2–7 days) depending on provider and snapshot indexing. We will include the deletion request id and provider-provided confirmation as evidence.

3) Expedited/contractual options:
- Expedited backup purge SLA (contract option): guaranteed initiation of backup purge within 24 hours and confirmation of purge within 7 calendar days. This is documented as an SLA and we can add automated purge confirmation to your security portal for evidence.

4) Logs and retention:
- Application logs: default 90 days (configurable).
- Audit/security logs: default 365 days. We can stream audit logs to your SIEM (SAML/secure syslog or HTTPS ingestion) for the contract period prior to any deletion — export can be configured as part of onboarding.

5) Evidence and artifacts:
- We maintain an internal backup_workflow_diagram.png and retention_matrix.csv (attached) showing the lifecycle and purge pipeline.
- SOC 2 reports and KMS key rotation logs are available under NDA.

Next steps for us: we can populate your vendor questionnaire (we prefer a secure form link/DocuSign). If you confirm expedited purge (7-day contractual SLA) we'll provide concrete language to add to the MSA and the evidence hooks (webhook/callback) to notify you when purge completes.

Attachments: backup_workflow_diagram.png, retention_matrix.csv

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
